decision: SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST — Iterative decompression restores decompression-normalization under double-brotli encoding for ALL auth states and under triple-brotli encoding for error states (no_auth/expired_token/invalid_token) on localhost mock server with deterministic brotli quality 6. reason: The frozen decision rule passes on observed data: all 9 conditions achieve discrimination 0.5 >= 0.3, all_same=true, B-RANDOM=0.0, all 6 encoding scenarios observed for error states. However, audit V1 (severity high) identified a systematic RNG defect: valid_token never experienced triple-br (0/180 reps across all 9 conditions) due to shared proxy-test draw consuming one RNG draw before the measured plan, shifting triple-br draws away from valid_token positions. This means triple-br for the distinct success body (the only body that separates valid_token from error collapse) is UNTESTED, not validated. The claim ceiling is therefore bounded: double-brotli survival established for all states, triple-brotli survival established for error states only. The audit V6 confirms all recomputed metrics match producer on observed data. No infrastructure failure — this is a sampling design limitation, not a measurement invalidity.
